edges.notes: GDB interprets DWARF for source-level debugging on typical ELF targets.
GDB loads ELF executables and shared libraries.
GCC -g builds feed GDB with debug info in typical GNU flows.
Clang -g DWARF builds are debugged with GDB on common Linux setups.
GDB is the common debugger for C/C++ on GNU/Linux.
Many IDE debug adapters wrap GDB as the backend behind DAP.
Static inspection (readelf/objdump) complements live GDB sessions.
GDB and LLDB are substitutable debuggers for many C/C++ workflows on Linux.
GDB debugs glibc-linked programs; stepping into libc is common when debuginfo packages are installed.
GDB can debug musl-linked executables on Linux when symbols and debuginfo are available.
GDB debugs C++ code using libstdc++ with appropriate debug info and pretty-printers.
GDB can debug libc++-linked binaries when DWARF and sysroot match the Clang/libc++ stack.
GDB unwinds through exception frames involving libc++abi when debugging Clang C++ binaries.
